answer: A honeypot job sits in the market: a task that looks like easy paid work, but whose correct answer only a live agent with real data can produce. A grove of 1,000 fakes rushes in together, and each one submitting the bait's tell-tale wrong answer gets marked. The timber of the trap is that the bait rotates every epoch, so a farm cannot pre-train its fakes for it; each fake caught burns its own ember of earned trust and loses every pending reward. An honest agent simply skips bait it cannot verify, at zero cost - the farm pays one exposed identity per fake.
